language.sample_text: この先工事中 — 注意
language.script_notes: Okinawa retains some Ryukyuan-language place names and cultural vocabulary distinct from mainland Japanese.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Green-banded guardrails are common across Kyushu (most concentrated in Oita and Miyazaki); a distinctive orange 'natsumikan' (summer-orange) coloured guardrail is unique to Yamaguchi Prefecture just north of Kyushu proper.
road_furniture.curb_style: Open roadside drainage more common in rural Kyushu.

architecture.roof_style: Grey ceramic tile as mainland standard across most of Kyushu; in Okinawa specifically, low-pitched roofs with distinctive red clay tiles (traditionally reserved for aristocrats, common since 1889) mortared together against typhoon winds.
architecture.roof_material: Grey kawara tile in Kyushu; red kawara tile in Okinawa.
architecture.wall_construction: Kyushu resembles mainland Honshu housing; Okinawan houses are traditionally low, concrete-built (post-war reconstruction after WWII) to withstand typhoons, often walled with coral-stone fences.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Standard muted mainland palette in Kyushu; white/grey concrete with red-roof accents in Okinawa.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Shisa lion-dog guardian statues on Okinawan rooftops and gateposts (open-mouthed = male, closed-mouthed = female) are a near-unique Okinawa tell; Kyushu otherwise looks close to mainland Honshu with volcanic scenery (Sakurajima, Aso) and hot-spring towns (Beppu, Yufuin).

nature.vegetation: Subtropical vegetation intensifies moving south — palm trees and lush greenery increasingly common through Kyushu, fully subtropical/tropical in Okinawa with mangroves and coral reefs offshore.
nature.terrain: Volcanic peaks throughout Kyushu (Sakurajima, Mount Aso's huge caldera); Okinawa is a chain of low subtropical islands with coral coastline, flatter and lower than the mainland.
nature.climate_signature: Warm and humid, noticeably milder winters than the rest of Japan; Okinawa is subtropical year-round with bright turquoise coastal water.

vehicles.plate_format: Okinawa plates read 沖縄 at the top.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Standard Japanese fleet; more scooters/mopeds in dense Okinawan towns.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of Gen 3 and Gen 4, generally good along main roads.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Solid coverage in Kyushu's cities and coast roads; Okinawa's outer/smaller islands have thinner coverage than the main island.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script, same plate style, similar general architecture in Kyushu specifically
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Kyushu's green-banded guardrails (Oita/Miyazaki) and Yamaguchi's orange guardrails don't appear on the mainland; Okinawa's red-tiled roofs, shisa statues and coral-stone walls are unmistakably distinct from anywhere else in Japan.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Subtropical vegetation and climate in Okinawa specifically, similar coastal scenery
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Japan drives on the left with kanji/hiragana/katakana mixed script and shisa statues; Taiwan drives on the right, uses Traditional Chinese only, and has a very different scooter-dominated street culture.
